Every cell contains the same fixed set of shapes; any other shapes are noise with no system.

Every box contains one hollow square, two solid pentagons.

Other figures may also be present, but nothing governs them: neither their type, their fill nor their position.

Only one option contains exactly one hollow square, two solid pentagons; the others break the fixed set.

1: changes the fill of the pentagons, which is part of the fixed set
2: lacks one hollow square that every cell must contain
3: keeps only the stray shapes and drops the fixed set
4: has one hollow square too many
5: changes the fill of the square, which is part of the fixed set

Two things matter: how many shapes a cell holds, and which shapes appear for that number.

Across each row the number of shapes falls by 1.

Down each column the number of shapes rises by 1. The shapes are nested: a cell with n shapes shows the first n of a fixed order (1: + star, 2: + hexagon, 3: + triangle, 4: + pentagon, 5: + square).

The missing cell needs 3 shapes: one hollow hexagon, one hollow star and one hollow triangle.

2: has two shapes too many
3: has one shape too few
4: has the right number of shapes but the wrong mix
5: changes a fill
6: has the right number of shapes but includes a shape that only appears in larger sets

The missing cell needs 3 shapes: one hollow pentagon, one hollow star and one hollow triangle.

1: has the right number of shapes but the wrong mix
2: has two shapes too many
3: has the right number of shapes but includes a shape that only appears in larger sets
5: changes a fill
6: has one shape too few

The rows are transformations of one another: the bottom row is the top row transformed.

Row 3 is row 1 mirrored top to bottom, cell by cell.

Row 2 is row 1 mirrored left to right.

Take the top-right cell and apply the same transformation: mirrored top to bottom.

1: applies the wrong transformation to the top cell (rotated 90° anticlockwise)
2: copies the top cell of the column unchanged
3: copies the cell to the left
5: applies the wrong transformation to the top cell (rotated 90° clockwise)
6: applies the wrong transformation to the top cell (mirrored left to right)
